```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(leaflet)
library(flexdashboard)

source("R/site_helpers.R")

# TODO (team): swap the demo files for the real outputs of Q1, Q2 and the estimator
hospital_medians =
  read_csv("data/demo_hospital_medians.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(condition = fct_relevel(condition, condition_levels)) |>
  group_by(condition) |>
  mutate(ratio = median_charges / median(median_charges[n_stays >= min_cases])) |>
  ungroup()

estimator_grid =
  read_csv("data/demo_estimator_grid.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

dollar = scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1)

site_layout = function(p, ...) {
  p |>
    layout(
      font = list(family = "Inter, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif", color = site_ink, size = 13),
      paper_bgcolor = site_paper,
      plot_bgcolor = site_paper,
      margin = list(l = 70, r = 30, t = 20, b = 60),
      hoverlabel = list(bgcolor = "white", bordercolor = site_rule, font = list(color = site_ink)),
      ...
    ) |>
    config(displayModeBar = FALSE)
}

# Hospitals ranked by median charge, with interval bars
ranking_plot = function(condition_name) {
  plot_data =
    hospital_medians |>
    filter(condition == condition_name, n_stays >= min_cases) |>
    mutate(
      rank = min_rank(median_charges),
      hover = str_c(
        "<b>", facility_name, "</b><br>", region, " · ", ownership,
        "<br>Median charge: ", dollar(median_charges),
        "<br>95% interval: ", dollar(charges_low), " to ", dollar(charges_high),
        "<br>Stays: ", n_stays
      )
    )

  typical_value = median(plot_data$median_charges)

  plot_ly(
    plot_data,
    x = ~median_charges, y = ~rank,
    type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
    marker = list(color = ~ratio_colour(ratio), size = 7, line = list(color = site_ink, width = 0.4)),
    error_x = list(
      type = "data", symmetric = FALSE,
      array = ~charges_high - median_charges, arrayminus = ~median_charges - charges_low,
      color = site_rule, thickness = 1, width = 0
    ),
    text = ~hover, hoverinfo = "text"
  ) |>
    site_layout(
      xaxis = list(title = "Median charge per stay (log scale)", type = "log", tickprefix = "$", gridcolor = site_rule),
      yaxis = list(title = "Hospitals, lowest to highest", showticklabels = FALSE, showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE),
      shapes = list(list(
        type = "line", x0 = typical_value, x1 = typical_value, yref = "paper", y0 = 0, y1 = 1,
        line = list(color = site_blue, dash = "dot", width = 1)
      ))
    )
}

# Median cost against number of stays; uses every hospital
funnel_plot = function(condition_name) {
  plot_data =
    hospital_medians |>
    filter(condition == condition_name) |>
    mutate(
      enough = if_else(n_stays >= min_cases, "30 or more stays", "Fewer than 30 stays"),
      hover = str_c("<b>", facility_name, "</b><br>Stays: ", n_stays, "<br>Median cost: ", dollar(median_costs))
    )

  typical_value = median(plot_data$median_costs[plot_data$n_stays >= min_cases])

  plot_ly(
    plot_data,
    x = ~n_stays, y = ~median_costs,
    type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
    color = ~enough, colors = c("30 or more stays" = site_blue, "Fewer than 30 stays" = "#AEB8C2"),
    marker = list(size = 7, opacity = 0.8),
    text = ~hover, hoverinfo = "text"
  ) |>
    site_layout(
      xaxis = list(title = "Number of stays (log scale)", type = "log", gridcolor = site_rule),
      yaxis = list(title = "Median estimated cost (log scale)", type = "log", tickprefix = "$", gridcolor = site_rule),
      legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.2),
      shapes = list(
        list(type = "line", xref = "paper", x0 = 0, x1 = 1, y0 = typical_value, y1 = typical_value, line = list(color = site_teal, dash = "dot", width = 1)),
        list(type = "line", x0 = min_cases, x1 = min_cases, yref = "paper", y0 = 0, y1 = 1, line = list(color = site_muted, dash = "dot", width = 1))
      )
    )
}

# The same typical patient at every hospital: one dot per hospital, sorted from the
# lowest predicted charge to the highest. The menu on the chart switches the patient.
estimator_plot = function(condition_name) {
  plot_data =
    estimator_grid |>
    filter(condition == condition_name) |>
    group_by(profile) |>
    mutate(rank = min_rank(predicted_charges)) |>
    ungroup()

  # patients in order of how costly they are, the least costly first
  profiles =
    plot_data |>
    group_by(profile) |>
    summarize(typical = median(predicted_charges)) |>
    arrange(typical) |>
    pull(profile)

  # for each patient: the 10th and 90th percentile hospital, and how far apart they are
  spread =
    plot_data |>
    group_by(profile) |>
    summarize(
      p10 = quantile(predicted_charges, 0.1),
      p90 = quantile(predicted_charges, 0.9),
      n_hospitals = n()
    ) |>
    mutate(note = str_c("Same patient: the 90th-percentile hospital charges ", round(p90 / p10, 1), "× the 10th (", n_hospitals, " hospitals)"))

  # dotted lines and the sentence for one patient profile
  profile_layout = function(profile_name) {
    row = spread |> filter(profile == profile_name)
    list(
      shapes = map(unname(c(row$p10, row$p90)), \(x) {
        list(type = "line", x0 = x, x1 = x, yref = "paper", y0 = 0, y1 = 1, line = list(color = site_teal, dash = "dot", width = 1))
      }),
      annotations = list(list(
        text = row$note, xref = "paper", yref = "paper", x = 1, y = 0.02, xanchor = "right",
        showarrow = FALSE, font = list(color = site_ink, size = 13)
      ))
    )
  }

  p = plot_ly()

  for (profile_name in profiles) {
    p =
      p |>
      add_markers(
        data = plot_data |> filter(profile == profile_name),
        x = ~predicted_charges, y = ~rank,
        marker = list(color = site_blue, size = 7, opacity = 0.85),
        text = ~str_c("<b>", facility_name, "</b><br>", region, " · ", ownership, "<br>Predicted charge: ", dollar(predicted_charges)),
        hoverinfo = "text",
        visible = profile_name == profiles[1],
        showlegend = FALSE
      )
  }

  profile_buttons =
    map(profiles, \(profile_name) {
      list(
        method = "update",
        args = list(list(visible = as.list(profiles == profile_name)), profile_layout(profile_name)),
        label = profile_name
      )
    })

  first = profile_layout(profiles[1])

  p |>
    site_layout(
      xaxis = list(title = "Predicted charge for this patient (log scale)", type = "log", tickprefix = "$", gridcolor = site_rule),
      yaxis = list(title = "Hospitals, lowest to highest", showticklabels = FALSE, showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE),
      shapes = first$shapes,
      annotations = first$annotations,
      updatemenus = list(list(
        buttons = profile_buttons, active = 0,
        x = 0.02, xanchor = "left", y = 0.98, yanchor = "top"
      ))
    )
}
```

Overview
=====================================

Row {data-height=140}
-------------------------------------

### Hospitals with 30+ stays in at least one condition

```{r}
hospital_medians |>
  filter(n_stays >= min_cases) |>
  distinct(hosp_id) |>
  nrow() |>
  valueBox(caption = "hospitals compared (demo data)")
```

### Stays

```{r}
hospital_medians |>
  summarize(n = sum(n_stays)) |>
  pull(n) |>
  scales::label_comma()() |>
  valueBox(caption = "stays across five conditions (demo data)")
```

### Gap

```{r}
hospital_medians |>
  filter(n_stays >= min_cases) |>
  group_by(condition) |>
  summarize(gap = quantile(median_charges, 0.9) / quantile(median_charges, 0.1)) |>
  summarize(gap = max(gap)) |>
  pull(gap) |>
  round(1) |>
  str_c("×") |>
  valueBox(caption = "largest 90th ÷ 10th percentile gap in median charges (demo data)")
```

### Markup

```{r}
hospital_medians |>
  filter(n_stays >= min_cases) |>
  summarize(markup = median(markup)) |>
  pull(markup) |>
  round(1) |>
  str_c("×") |>
  valueBox(caption = "typical charge-to-cost ratio (demo data)")
```

Row
-------------------------------------

### Hospitals by condition: charges relative to the typical hospital {data-width=680}

```{r}
heatmap_data =
  hospital_medians |>
  group_by(hosp_id) |>
  mutate(total_stays = sum(n_stays), mean_log_ratio = mean(log(ratio[n_stays >= min_cases]))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(dense_rank(desc(total_stays)) <= 40) |>
  mutate(
    facility_name = fct_reorder(facility_name, mean_log_ratio),
    z = if_else(n_stays >= min_cases, log2(ratio), NA_real_),
    hover = if_else(
      n_stays >= min_cases,
      str_c("<b>", facility_name, "</b><br>", condition, "<br>", round(ratio, 2), "× the typical hospital<br>Stays: ", n_stays),
      str_c("<b>", facility_name, "</b><br>", condition, "<br>Too few cases (", n_stays, ")")
    )
  )

plot_ly(
  heatmap_data,
  x = ~condition, y = ~facility_name, z = ~z,
  type = "heatmap",
  zmin = -1.5, zmax = 1.5,
  colorscale = list(c(0, site_low), c(0.5, site_mid), c(1, site_high)),
  xgap = 3, ygap = 2,
  text = ~hover, hoverinfo = "text",
  colorbar = list(title = "", tickvals = c(-1, 0, 1), ticktext = c("half", "typical", "double"), len = 0.5, thickness = 12)
) |>
  site_layout(
    plot_bgcolor = site_grey_cell,
    xaxis = list(title = "", side = "top"),
    yaxis = list(title = "", showticklabels = FALSE),
    margin = list(l = 20, r = 20, t = 40, b = 20)
  )
```

### How to read this {data-width=320 .how-to}

#### Is it the hospital, or the condition?

Each row is a hospital and each column is a condition. Darker cells are above the typical hospital for that condition, lighter cells are below. The typical hospital is the median of the hospital medians, not the median of all stays.

- Rows that stay dark are consistently expensive; rows that stay light are consistently cheap.
- Rows that mix dark and light are expensive for some conditions only.
- Grey cells have fewer than 30 stays, too few to compare.

The 40 hospitals with the most stays are shown, sorted from the most expensive on average (top) to the least.

<p class="small-note"><span class="demo-badge">Demo</span> Simulated data. Charges are billed amounts, not what patients paid.</p>

### How to read this {.how-to}

#### How far apart are hospitals?

Each dot is a hospital's median charge for one condition. The bar is its 95% bootstrap interval: a short bar means we are fairly sure where the hospital sits.

The dotted line is the typical hospital: the median of the hospital medians. Hover over a dot for the hospital's name and numbers.

Only hospitals with at least 30 stays for the condition are shown.

<p class="small-note"><span class="demo-badge">Demo</span> Simulated data.</p>

### How to read this {.how-to}

#### Real outlier, or small numbers?

Small hospitals swing widely by chance; large hospitals should sit close to the typical hospital (horizontal line). A large hospital far from the line is worth a second look.

This view shows every hospital, including those with fewer than 30 stays (grey, left of the vertical line).

<p class="small-note"><span class="demo-badge">Demo</span> Simulated data. Costs are the state's estimates.</p>

Map
=====================================

Row
-------------------------------------

### Hospitals in New York State {data-width=720}

```{r}
map_data =
  hospital_medians |>
  filter(condition == "Heart failure", n_stays >= min_cases, !is.na(latitude))

leaflet(map_data) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~longitude, lat = ~latitude,
    radius = ~pmin(3 + sqrt(n_stays) / 4, 14),
    stroke = TRUE, color = site_ink, weight = 0.6,
    fillColor = ~ratio_colour(ratio), fillOpacity = 0.9,
    popup = ~str_c("<b>", facility_name, "</b><br>", region, "<br>Median charge: ", dollar(median_charges), "<br>", round(ratio, 2), "× the typical hospital")
  )
```

### How to read this {data-width=280 .how-to}

#### Where are the expensive hospitals?

Each circle is a hospital. Colour shows its median charge for heart failure relative to the typical hospital (darker is higher, lighter is lower); size shows the number of stays. Click a circle for details.

Hospitals without coordinates in the state facility file are not shown.

<p class="small-note"><span class="demo-badge">Demo</span> Simulated locations and values. TODO: add a condition selector.</p>

Column {data-width=280}
-------------------------------------

### How to read this {.how-to}

#### Same patient, different hospital

Choose a condition, then a typical patient with the menu on the chart. Each dot is one hospital's predicted charge for that same patient, from the lowest to the highest.

The two dotted lines mark the hospitals at the 10th and 90th percentile; the sentence under the chart says how far apart they are. Hover over a dot for the hospital's name.

Predictions come from the adjusted model. They are estimates of billed charges, not of what a patient would pay.

<p class="small-note"><span class="demo-badge">Demo</span> Simulated predictions.</p>
